descriptionChirho: As a gift, gratuitously, without charge or monetary cost; rendered 'freely' (eng), 'gratuitamente/gratis' (spa), 'मुफ़्त' (hin), 'مجّانًا' (arb), '거저' (kor), 'bure' (swa). Used of receiving or giving spiritual blessings without payment (Matt 10:8, Rom 3:24, 2 Cor 11:7, Rev 21:6, Rev 22:17), emphasizing the gracious, unearned nature of divine gifts across seven occurrences.

Without legitimate reason or just grounds, signifying an action performed against someone who has done nothing to merit it; rendered 'without cause' (eng), 'sin causa' (spa), 'बिना कारण' (hin), 'مَجَّانًا' (arb), '까닭 없이' (kor), 'bure' (swa). Used in John 15:25 quoting Psalm 35:19/69:4, where hatred directed at Jesus is characterized as groundless and unjustified. The Hindi and Korean translations especially clarify this causal rather than financial sense.

labelChirho: for nothing, in vain, to no purpose
descriptionChirho: To no effect, pointlessly, rendering an action purposeless or futile; rendered 'for nothing' (eng), 'en vano' (spa), 'व्यर्थ' (hin), 'باطلًا' (arb), '헛되이' (kor), 'bure' (swa). Used in Galatians 2:21 where Paul argues that if righteousness came through the law, then Christ died 'for nothing'—his death would have been purposeless. The Arabic باطلًا (vain/futile) and Spanish 'en vano' sharply distinguish this from the financial 'freely' or causal 'without reason' senses.
